pictures.strongest_point: The dense conifer forest around the clearing reads like real aerial drone footage: varied heights, believable dark spruce crowns and soft overcast light with no hard CG shadows.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The roads are pale, flat ribbons with perfectly parallel, evenly spaced rut lines and razor-clean edges. The thin white birch-like trees in the clearing are sparse stick props that look pasted on. The three hay mounds are smooth egg-shaped blobs. The round dome at the bottom is a featureless blob, and the grass of the clearing is one even, tidy carpet.

pictures.strongest_point: The house textures (thatch, timber frame, stone) are detailed for a game asset, and the shadows are consistent with one sun.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Unmistakable low-poly game look: faceted polygon tree crowns, lollipop trees on straight stick trunks and stacked-cone pines. The mountains are smooth gradient humps against an empty flat sky. The sandy ground is tiled, with no grass blades, and the grass has a sharp straight edge against the sand. The haystack in the foreground is a smooth blob, and the scale feels toy-like.

pictures.strongest_point: Sunny light with atmospheric haze, varied forest colour (some autumn patches, bare earth under the trees) and believable rutted tracks give a natural overall layout.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The forest canopy is soft, rounded leaf clumps that look painterly or game-like rather than real foliage. The trees in the clearing are near-identical round lollipop shapes that repeat, with heavy, uniformly dark shadow blobs. The grass is a light green carpet with blotchy repeating speckles. The houses are tiny and clean, and a bare dead tree in the foreground looks like a flat cut-out.

pictures.strongest_point: Strong aerial perspective: misty, hazy depth down the lane, nice back-lit grass with small flowers, and wet ruts catching the sky.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The big conifer on the right has a combed, stripy texture like stacked fern cards, which is an obvious CG tree. The cottage roof is smooth clay or plastic with drawn-on stripes in the gable. The walls are clean and toy-like. The brown ground at bottom left shows a repeating cobble-like tile pattern. The pebbles are evenly sprinkled and the puddle reflections look smeared.

pictures.strongest_point: The tall dry meadow grass on both sides is very photographic, and the dark mixed forest, birches and cloudy sky make a believable backdrop.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The road is a too-smooth, too-clean sand plane, edged by grey smooth berms that look modelled. The puddle in the ruts is a flat, saturated blue patch like paint rather than water. The footprints look stamped on. The thatch is a soft, mushy, uniform mass, and the light is a little flat.

pictures.strongest_point: The buildings themselves (thatch, red timber frame, stone hut) have reasonable textures and sit on the ground.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Low-poly faceted trees and cone pines sit against a flat green backdrop wall and an empty gradient sky. The road ruts look like rope or caterpillar ridges with a smeared, stretched texture, and the water lies in dark straight strips. Sparse single-sprout weeds are spaced evenly over flat ground, and arched stalks look like wires. The haystack is a blob.

pictures.strongest_point: The roof shingles have some moss colour variation, and the open door adds a little depth.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Half the frame is foreground ground with a heavily stretched, swirly bark-like texture and grey blotches, which nothing in nature looks like. The trees are low-poly faceted crowns, one an umbrella-like flat disc on a pole. There is a flat green backdrop wall and an empty sky. The stone plinth has cartoon outlines, the shingle pattern repeats, and the lighting is flat.

pictures.strongest_point: Rich, lived-in composition: a detailed timber barn with an open stall, a believable cart with spoked wheels, barrels and hazy background trees in soft daylight.
pictures.most_visible_faults: All the wood is one clean, uniform grey-beige with no weathering, dirt or rot. The foreground grass is evenly spaced clumps standing on a bare smooth green plane. The dirt yard is smooth and clean. The conifer at left has the combed, stripy CG look, and some leaves float in the sky against the top of the tree mass.

pictures.strongest_point: The background of tall dark spruces under a sky with clouds is highly convincing, and the curving wheel tracks in the yard look natural.
pictures.most_visible_faults: There is an odd pure-black hole shape in the foreground puddle and a dark smudgy blob shadow under the rail. The yard is a smooth clay surface with evenly scattered round green-grey pebbles like polka dots. The haystack is a smooth dome blob. The roof slates are very evenly tiled with flat moss patches, and the wood is clean and uniform.

pictures.strongest_point: The overgrown tall meadow grass in the foreground and the realistic spruces against a cloud-flecked sky are close to photographic, and the half-timbered proportions feel right.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The thatch is a smoothly streaked, brushed texture with a sausage-like eave, and stray straw strands float in front of the walls like fuzz or sparkles. The walls are clean white panels with faint streaks. The timbers and barrel are clean and unweathered. The shutters are flat, and the dark window recess is uniform black.

pictures.strongest_point: Fibrous thatch, a log pile, rail fence, stone steps and a flower-filled meadow make a warm, plausible cottage scene with good hazy depth.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The tree on the right is made of large flat leaf cards that read clearly as CG. Small flowers are sprinkled very evenly across the grass. The thatch is uniform and soft with no wear at the ridge, the stone steps are clean blocks, the timbers are one flat grey-brown, and the plaster blotches look painted on.

pictures.strongest_point: The stone well with its bucket, rope and wooden frame has a convincing stone texture and sits solidly on the ground.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The trees are low-poly faceted crowns on stick trunks, behind them a flat green backdrop wall. The plaster panels have cartoon wavy outlines, and the thatch is a flat orange texture. The ground is flat and blotchy with sparse, evenly spaced single sprouts, the sacks are lumpy blobs, and the sky is empty.

pictures.strongest_point: Lots of small-scale story (thin puddles reflecting the sky, scattered leaves and twigs, dappled sunlight) gives it a lively, real-feeling light.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The pebbles are near-identical round sweets, evenly scattered. The mud is soft and smeared, with a stretched low-resolution look, and the rut edges are smooth moulded clay. The grass blades are big, flat, saturated green cards, and the fern at top right is an obvious flat card. The puddle edges are smeared.

pictures.strongest_point: The thatch and timber houses in the background are reasonably textured.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The road fills the frame with a badly stretched, smeared rock texture and grey slab facets. The ruts are filled with flat grey strips of 'water' that have no reflection or depth. A few lone sprouts stand like stickers. The trees are low-poly faceted, behind them a flat green backdrop wall, and the sky is empty.

pictures.strongest_point: The tall dry grass at the verges is very photographic, and the elongated puddle in the rut reflecting the blue sky looks natural; the overall colours are muted and believable.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The sand is unnaturally smooth and clean, like plaster or beach sand, with no fine grit, mud or organic debris. Small grey pebbles are evenly sprinkled. The ruts are soft, rounded grooves with a dark smear, and two sets of tracks loop oddly. A smooth greenish berm runs along the edges, and the footprints look stamped in.

best_per_view.why: Its conifer forest and soft overcast light read most like a real drone photo. C's canopy is soft and painterly, with repeated lollipop trees, and B is plainly low-poly. A's flaws (painted-looking roads, blob hay mounds, stick birches) are smaller in the frame.

The tall meadow grass, mixed forest and cloudy sky are close to photographic. A's stripy conifer and plastic roof give it away faster, even with its nicer haze, and C is low-poly. B's main tells are the over-clean sand road and the flat blue puddle.

A believable barn, cart and barrels with no single glaring artefact. C has better background spruces, but the black hole in its foreground puddle and its polka-dot pebbles jump out. A is low-poly with a stretched swirly ground.
The wild meadow grass, sky and spruces are the most photographic in the whole set. B is close but let down by flat leaf-card trees and evenly sprinkled flowers, and C is low-poly.

Natural muted colours, real-looking verge grass and a plausible sky-reflecting puddle. A is livelier but its candy-like pebbles, smeared mud and bright flat grass cards look more game-like. B is a stretched-texture low-poly render.

results.overall_note: All 15 pictures are 1200x800 and were judged at full size. In every view one maker's picture is plainly a low-poly game render: faceted polygon trees, a flat green backdrop wall, an empty gradient sky, stretched smeared ground textures and evenly spaced lone sprouts. Those never pass as photographs (1.5 to 2.5). The other two makers are in a closer 5 to 6.5 band. Their real strengths are tall meadow grass, convincing spruce forests, haze and sky, but they share recurring give-aways: surfaces that are too clean and smooth (sand roads, clay mud, unweathered wood and plaster), evenly scattered round identical pebbles, combed or stripy conifers and flat leaf-card trees, smooth blob haystacks and hay mounds, thatch that looks brushed or mushy (with floating stray straws in one case), and puddles that read as flat blue paint or black holes. None would survive a close look as a real photograph. The best few (cottage 4A, eye-level road 2B, aerial 1A) could pass at a glance or as a small thumbnail. The quickest realism gains would come from dirtier, weathered, irregular surfaces, random rather than even scatter, and fixing the tree cards and puddle shading.

pictures.strongest_point: Strongest forest of the overhead views: a thick wall of spruce and broadleaf closes in on all sides, so it clearly sits in a forest clearing. The cottages read as thatched and half-timbered, and there are hay ricks in a fenced paddock.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The roads look kept, not unkept: wide, pale and smooth, with ruler-straight edges and two thin dark rut lines running the whole length like tram rails. No mud, puddles or weeds show in the track. The grass looks like mown lawn. Isolated white birches stand oddly alone in the field. No building clearly reads as the stable, and the props are too small to read.

pictures.strongest_point: The buildings read as mediaeval: a thatched half-timbered longhouse, a red-brick half-timber cottage, a stone cottage with a mossy roof, a well, barrels and a haystack.
pictures.most_visible_faults: It is not in a forest. It is an open field with one row of faceted low-poly trees, a bare sandy plane behind them and painted mountains. There is a hard seam where the grass ground meets the sand ground. The road is a flat brown painted strip with faint lines, with no depth, mud or puddles. The haystack in the foreground is cut off by the frame.

pictures.strongest_point: The tracks look the most organically worn from above: narrow, curving, branching dirt roads with visible ruts, and bare dirt patches where they meet doorways and yards. The whole clearing is ringed by a convincing mixed forest.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The cottages are small, generic brown boxes with grey roofs, so they barely read as mediaeval and none clearly reads as a stable. The roads are still fairly clean, with no puddles or muddy patches visible. The grass is a bright, uniform blotchy green, and the round lollipop trees in the clearing look placed.

pictures.strongest_point: The most truly unkept road in the set: two muddy wheel ruts filled with water that reflects the sky, a weedy grass crown between them, stones, twigs and wet churned edges. It winds into a hazy forest past cottages with fences and barrels.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The cottage roof looks like smooth clay or plaster, not thatch. The big pine on the right has a combed, striped needle artefact. The bottom-left ground has an odd scaly, tiled brown pattern. No hoof prints are visible.

pictures.strongest_point: The only eye-level road with a line of hoof prints down the centre between the two wheel ruts, which is exactly where a horse pulling a cart would walk. Standing water lies in the ruts. A properly mediaeval half-timbered thatched cottage, a well and a small open shed sit against a dense forest.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The road surface is pale, dry and smooth like packed sand, with little real mud. The puddle is a flat, over-saturated blue sheet that looks pasted on. The road banks are smooth grey-green slopes with no texture.

pictures.strongest_point: The buildings along the road still read as mediaeval: thatch, half-timbering, a stone cottage, barrels and a haystack.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The road reads as a ploughed field or a pair of drainage ditches, not a cart track: deep straight trenches with a stretched bark-like texture and thin water strips. The weeds are evenly spaced seedling sprigs. The trees are faceted low-poly blobs, with a painted green backdrop and mountains, so it is not a forest. The ground on either side is flat and empty.

pictures.strongest_point: A plausible plank-and-wattle shed on a stone footing, with a mossy shingle roof and open plank doors.
pictures.most_visible_faults: It does not read as a stable: the interior is dark, with no stalls, mangers or tack visible, so it could be any shed. The foreground yard has a smeared, stretched bark texture with grey patches, not hoof-churned mud. The background is a flat sandy plane with low-poly trees and a painted hill backdrop, so it is not a forest. The only props are a couple of barrels.

pictures.strongest_point: A believable timber barn with open bays, a hay-hoist beam and rope at the gable, barrels, and a two-wheeled cart parked in front, which gives the horse-and-carriage cue. It is clearly empty, with trees close behind.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The bays show plank walls but no clear stalls, mangers or hay racks, so it reads as a cart shed as much as a stable. The yard dirt is clean, flat and pale, with no ruts, hoof prints, dung or straw. The foreground grass clumps look like cartoon cards.

pictures.strongest_point: The most believable empty stable: open-fronted, with visible empty stall partitions, stable half-doors, a hitching rail, a bucket, a trough and dung on the ground. Curved wheel tracks run past a cart, a haystack stands nearby, and a dense conifer forest rises behind.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The puddle in front looks like a black hole in the ground, not water. The dirt is a uniform beige, sprinkled evenly with greenish pebbles like polka dots. The moss on the roof is blotchy flat spotting.

pictures.strongest_point: Strongly mediaeval: whitewashed half-timbering with diagonal braces, a thick thatch with a ridge, a stone chimney, plank shutters, a barred window, a bench, a clay pot, a barrel, a wattle fence and a well. Forest stands behind.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Stray straw strands hang down across the white walls like scratches or hairs, and the thatch surface looks smeared and motion-blurred. The gable end is clad in modern-looking dark weatherboard. The plaster is too clean and new for an old cottage.

pictures.strongest_point: A cosy, lived-in cottage: thatch over daub-and-timber walls on a stone plinth, a log pile, a chopping stump, a bench, a barrel and stone steps. Wildflowers grow in the grass, the forest edge is behind, and an outbuilding stands in the background.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The thatch texture is stretched into streaky, brushed-fabric lines. The clay chimney pot and the neat post-and-rail fence feel later than mediaeval. The windows are dark and hard to read. The tree on the right shows big flat leaf cards.

pictures.strongest_point: Good mediaeval props: a stone well with a windlass, rope and wooden bucket, sacks and barrels, beside a thatched half-timbered longhouse.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The trees are faceted low-poly blobs over a painted green wall with a visible brown seam, so it is not a forest. The ground is flat, bare and dotted with seedling-like weed sprigs. The plaster has cartoon swirl cracks. The road on the left is a stretched bark texture.

pictures.strongest_point: A classic, neglected cart track: two wheel ruts holding water, a raised grass-and-weed crown down the middle, displaced muddy soil, stones, fallen leaves and twigs. Overgrown grass edges lead to a stone cottage and fence.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The pebbles are uniform rounded bean shapes, scattered evenly. There are no distinct hoof prints. Away from the ruts the soil looks dry and slightly smeared, more dust than mud. The water in the ruts is thin and streaky.

pictures.strongest_point: The village behind is at least recognisably mediaeval, with thatch and half-timbering.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The road surface fails at close range. The ruts are square trenches holding flat, untextured grey strips instead of water. The soil is a stretched, smeared bark or wood-chip texture that reads as a ploughed bed. The weeds are lone cartoon sprigs. Low-poly trees and a backdrop sit behind.

pictures.strongest_point: Shows horse-and-cart use: several curving, branching wheel ruts as if carts had turned, a puddle in one rut reflecting the sky, a run of hoof-like prints on the left, and pebbles and grass tufts.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The surface is pale, smooth beach-like sand, with no mud colour or wetness apart from the puddle. The puddle is a hard-edged, over-saturated blue cut-out. The ruts have a smooth, uniform profile like tyre tracks. The banks are smooth untextured grey-green slopes.

best_per_view.why: Narrowly ahead of A. Its tracks curve, branch and wear into bare dirt at the yards and doorways, which reads far more 'unkept' than A's straight, pale, rail-like roads, and it is just as clearly set in a forest. A has better mediaeval cottages, but the request leads with the roads. B is not in a forest at all.

The most unkept, wet and weedy road: muddy rutted tracks with water and a grass crown winding into the forest. B is close because of its hoof prints and its more mediaeval cottage, but its road is dry, pale sand with a pasted-on puddle. C's road looks like a ploughed field.

The only stable that is plainly a stable and plainly empty: visible empty stalls, half-doors, a hitching rail, a trough and bucket, dung, and a cart with wheel tracks, set against a dense forest. B is a good barn with a cart but shows no stalls and a clean yard. A is a dark shed on a flat plane.

A believable lived-in thatched cottage with the most fitting props (log pile, stump, bench, barrel, steps) and forest around it. A is just as mediaeval but is marred by straw hairs across the walls and a smeared thatch. C has a nice well but low-poly trees and bare ground.

The truest neglected horse-and-cart track at close range: wet ruts, a weedy crown, churned soil, stones and leaves. C has hoof prints and turning ruts but looks like smooth beach sand with a cut-out puddle. B's trenches and flat grey water strips do not read as a road.

results.overall_note: The five low-poly pictures (1B, 2C, 3A, 4C, 5B) consistently miss the brief. There is no forest, only rows of faceted trees on a flat plane with a painted backdrop. The roads read as ploughed trenches with a stretched bark texture and flat water strips, and the stable is just a dark shed. Only the buildings and props carry a mediaeval feel. The realistic pictures all deliver a forest village, with differing strengths. The muddiest, weediest, most unkept roads are in 2A and 5A (wet ruts, grass crown, twigs), but no hoof prints show anywhere among them. Hoof prints and turning cart tracks appear only in 2B and 5C, and that road surface looks like clean, dry, pale sand with over-saturated pasted puddles. The best stable by far is 3C (empty stalls, hitching rail, dung, cart tracks), though its puddle reads as a black hole. Across the set, almost nothing combines mud, puddles, hoof prints and dung in one road. The horse side of 'driven down by horse and carriage' is under-delivered: hoof prints appear only in 2B and 5C, and dung only in 3C. Roads seen from above (1A, 1C) look far tidier than the close-ups promise.

pictures.strongest_point: The forest is the most photographic of the three aerials: dense spruce and broadleaf with real depth. The foreground trees frame the clearing, and the X-shaped crossroads gives a clear leading shape.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The clearing is an even dark-green lawn that looks mown, like a golf course, with no gardens, fields, woodpiles or bare yards. The paired thin rut lines read as railway or tram tracks, not wheel ruts. The houses are tiny, spotless and few for the size of the clearing. The lone birches are thin and sparse, like planted saplings. A round domed object at bottom centre is half hidden by a conifer and reads as a mistake. The light is soft and flat, with little mood.

pictures.strongest_point: The buildings carry the most props of the three: timber framing, thatch, a well, barrels and sacks. A road with ruts runs through the scene.
pictures.most_visible_faults: It is a low-poly game look and unusable for a documentary. The trees are faceted lollipops planted in a single row, so this is not a forest village. A flat brown ground edge shows behind the tree line. The mountains are a smooth gradient, the sky is blank, and the sandy ground under the trees is an obviously tiled texture. The haystack cut off at the bottom edge looks accidental. The light is flat, like a game engine.

pictures.strongest_point: It has the most lived-in layout: more houses, fenced yards, worn paths leading to each door, a haystack, and bare brown earth under the forest canopy. There is some autumn colour in the trees.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The foliage is soft and blobby with low detail, and the trees in the clearing are cloned lollipop shapes. A bright haze washes out contrast so the image looks milky. The grass is a uniform pale green with speckles. The houses are very small and read as models. The composition is scattered, with no clear subject.

pictures.strongest_point: The best mood and depth of the eye-level views. A wet, rutted road with puddles reflecting the sky winds back through atmospheric haze past cottages at three distances, under warm low sun. Flowers in the verge and twigs in the mud add life.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The nearest cottage's roof is smooth putty with no thatch texture, and its walls are clean. The big conifer on the right has striped, comb-like needle cards that look plainly computer-made. The dirt at bottom left shows a repeating cobble-like pattern. The grass tufts sprinkled on the road look placed by hand. The sky is an empty gradient and the haze is a little heavy.

pictures.strongest_point: The surfaces are the most believable: the tall dry meadow grass looks real, there are footprints down the middle of the road, the thatch has a moss tint, and there are real clouds. The spruce and birch forest backdrop reads as a real forest edge.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The puddles are flat, over-saturated blue shapes that look painted on. The road edge is a sandy slab with a hard lip where the grass is stuck in. The cottage is awkwardly cut by the left frame edge, along with a stray fence post. The tree line is a dark, monotonous wall. The light is cool and flat, and the cottage walls are too clean.

pictures.strongest_point: The props are dressed: barrels, sacks, a haystack, a mix of house types. The road runs straight down the centre.
pictures.most_visible_faults: It is the same low-poly look: faceted trees and a flat green wall standing in for hills. The ruts look like ploughed ridges with grey water channels. Evenly spaced weed sprites stand on flat ground like seedlings in a nursery. The centred composition is dead. The light is flat, with no shadow modelling. The haystack is cut by the right edge.

pictures.strongest_point: The shingle roof has some moss patches, and the stable has a stone footing and open, hinged doors.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Half the frame is foreground ground covered in a huge swirling, smeared texture that is plainly out of scale and repeating. The trees are low-poly, including an umbrella-shaped tree at top left. A flat green backdrop shows a visible ground-plane horizon. The light is shadowless and flat. Nothing suggests animals or use: no straw, dung or hoof marks.

pictures.strongest_point: An attractive three-quarter composition with warm, hazy light. The cart leads the eye in, and barrels, a hitching rail and a stone block dress the yard. The mixed forest behind has autumn tints and depth.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The timber is uniformly new and clean, with no weathering, rot or staining. The yard has no mud, straw, dung or hoof prints at the stall doors. The foreground grass is a carpet of identical clumps on flat green ground. The shingles are too regular. The conifer at left shows striped needle cards.

pictures.strongest_point: The most weathered stable: a mossy shingle roof, half-doors to the stalls, posts on stone pads, a bucket, a cart, curved wheel ruts in the yard and a few droppings. The dense spruce backdrop is very convincing.
pictures.most_visible_faults: A black, hard-edged puddle in the bottom foreground reads as a hole in the ground. Even with it fixed, the pebbles are sprinkled like polka dots. A dark, blurry shadow sits under the rail. The walls are clean, even grey boards. The frontal, roof-cropped composition and the large empty yard are static.

pictures.strongest_point: A strong, sunlit half-timbered cottage with a barred window, shutters, a bench, a clay pot and a stone plinth. The tall wild meadow grass, the real-looking spruce backdrop and the clouds give it photographic presence.
pictures.most_visible_faults: Stray straws float in front of the walls below the eaves and read as specks. The thatch looks like motion-blurred fur. Uncut grass runs right up to the walls with no trodden ground at the door, so it reads as abandoned. The plaster is too clean. The roof is cut at top left and the barrel at bottom left, which looks unplanned.

pictures.strongest_point: The most lived-in close-up: a log pile, a chopping stump, stone steps, a bench, a barrel, worn bare earth at the door, a chimney with a pot, and stained plaster. The fence frames it, wildflowers fill the foreground, and a barn sits in the hazy depth. The warm light is pleasant.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The fence and timbers are clean and sharp-edged, as if new. The thatch looks combed, like fabric. The windows are black voids. The flowers are spread too evenly. The leaves on the right tree are large flat cards. The roof shows no sag, moss or repairs.

pictures.strongest_point: The stone well in the foreground is decently textured, with a rope, bucket and iron crank, and it gives the frame a foreground layer.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The trees are low-poly. The plaster walls carry a giant swirled crack pattern at the wrong scale. The ground is flat and dotted with evenly spaced sprouts. The rutted road at left shows an obvious tiled texture. A flat green backdrop stands behind with a visible ground edge. The thatch is patchy orange, and the light is flat game-engine light.

pictures.strongest_point: Warm, low sunlight with a soft background showing the village. Grass grows on the crown between the ruts, where it would, and fallen leaves and twigs sit in the mud. The left rut's water reflects the sky well.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The pebbles are round, uniform marbles resting on top of the dirt. The water in the right rut looks like frosted glass or a grey smear. The mud is smooth, clay-like blobs with no wet sheen at the edges. The grass blades are big, clean cards, so it looks stylized rather than photographic. The leaves are flat orange chips.

pictures.strongest_point: It keeps the village and buildings in the background, so the shot has context.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The road is a large, distorted bark-like noise texture, which is not believable as earth. The water in the ruts is flat grey plastic strips. The weed sprites are sparse and identical. There are low-poly trees and a flat green backdrop. The light is flat, and there is no wear, debris or footprints.

pictures.strongest_point: It reads most like a photograph of a used track. Branching rut geometry and foot or hoof depressions show traffic, tall dry grass verges look real, and a woodpile and fence sit in the background. The leading lines are strong.
pictures.most_visible_faults: The surface is too smooth and clean, like beach sand or concrete dust. The pebbles are sprinkled evenly. The puddle is a sharp-edged cutout in over-saturated blue. There is a hard grey-green band where the verge meets the road. The overall grade is greyish and flat, with little warmth, and no leaves, dung or twigs.

best_per_view.why: Its forest is the only one that would pass as real aerial footage, and the crossroads gives a readable composition. C has the more lived-in layout but soft, washed-out foliage. B is a low-poly game scene with a single row of trees.

It has the strongest light, haze and depth, a wet rutted road leading the eye past three layers of cottages, and flowers and twigs for life. B has more believable grass and footprints, but its painted-blue puddles, cropped house and flat light lose to A's mood. Both still need fixes: A's roof and stripy conifer, B's water.

It has the best composition and light, and a dressed yard with a cart, barrels and a rail. C has better weathering (mossy roof, ruts) but a glaring black-hole puddle and polka-dot pebbles in the foreground. A is unusable.

It is the most lived-in and best framed: a log pile, stump, steps, worn earth at the door, a fence foreground and hazy depth. A is equally photographic but sits in uncut grass with floating straws and an accidental crop.

Branching ruts, footprints and real dry grass verges read as a road people actually use, and the frame looks most like a photograph. A has nicer light and debris, but its marble pebbles, frosted-glass water and clay blobs look stylized.

results.overall_note: Two of the three looks could be used as a documentary backdrop after fixes; the third, the faceted low-poly look in 1B, 2C, 3A, 4C and 5B, could not. That one has repeating textures at the wrong scale, flat green backdrop walls, visible ground edges and shadowless light, and would need a full rebuild. The two realistic looks share the same remaining faults. Timber and plaster are too new and clean. Pebbles are scattered evenly, and puddles are sharp-edged cutouts or flat paint. Conifers show striped needle cards. Yards lack mud, straw, dung and trodden ground at doors. Before filming I would age all wood and plaster (stains, rot, moss at the base), soften water edges and add wet darkening around puddles, break up pebble and grass scatter, and add grass, mud and wear where people and animals walk. I would also crop with intent, and in the aerials give the clearing gardens, fields and woodpiles rather than lawn. Best usable frames: 4B, 2A, 3B and 5C.
